'''icebreath Chicken Noodle Soup''' is a [[Dark]] constructed list published on [[Game Players Network]].

== Deck info ==
* '''Player:''' [[David Kangas|icebreath]]
* '''Published:''' 3 November 2003 (Game Players Network)
* '''GPN category:''' Standard
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - Original VS3]]
* '''Side:''' [[Dark]]
* '''Starting Card:''' {{CardLink|Tatooine: Docking Bay 94|Premiere-D-tatooinedockingbay94.gif}}
* '''Strategy:''' Tatooine: Docking Bay 94
* '''GEMP Importable deck:''' [[Media:POVS3 Tatooine Docking Bay 94 icebreath.txt |Download]]

== Introduction ==

It's a million-to-one shot, but it just might work...

The published list has 62 cards.

== Strategy ==

Million-to-one chances crop up nine times out of ten.  Proven statistic.

This deck, like many that come out of my collection, is a pile.  Its design is unfamiliar, its play style is off the wall.  If anybody tries to make sense of it, odds are they'll either develop a facial twitch or go insane (often both).  Ah well, here goes:

The winning strat is to do some docking bay drains on Tatooine, enhanced by Fighters Coming In.  You're also getting in some direct damage through Search And Destroy and Tatooine Occupation.  The characters pulled by Ket Maliss are absolutely tech... Reegesk steals some cards to put under Hem, Dannik eats some soup, etc.

Meanwhile, a squadron of TIEs commanded by Darth Vader (V) guards the system.  With Vader subtracting from destiny draws (can you imagine him in combo with Zuckuss on Mist Hunter V?  *shiver*), Fel and Onyx Squadron adding destinies, plenty of immunity to go around, and Tallon Rolls a-plenty, you've pretty much got Tatooine to yourself.

There isn't a set way to play the deck... play whatever comes your way whenever and wherever you need it.  Questions?  Confusion?  Feel free to email me at kdavid@pacifier.com if you're having trouble bending your mind around something here.

Enjoy!

David Kangas

Shadow 31

Ophidian Agent

Vancouver, WA
